words.example: Use of solar power will benefit all mankind.

words.definition: unable to see or understand; to conceal; showing poor judgment or understanding
words.example: They were blind to the fact that they had little chance to succeed.
words.zh: 無法看見或理解；隱藏；表現出糟糕的判斷力或理解力

words.example: Education will broaden your opportunities to land a good job.
His talent as a pianist burgeoned at the age of 14.

words.definition: to perform a task, often for someone else
words.example: The boss required her team to carry out their plan.
words.zh: 執行一項任務，通常是為別人

words.example: His name was conspicuously absent from the list of winners.
A diet deficient in calcium can lead to bad health.
Successful politicians are usually eloquent speakers.
words.zh: 清晰、有效、令人信服地表達

words.example: The union endorsed the new contract.
His enormous wealth allows him to contribute to many charities.
The economist was entirely right in his analysis.
The senator's support is eroding because of his unpopular positions on the major issues.
The chances of the two sides reaching an agreement have evaporated.

words.definition: to get back; to have something returned
words.example: The NASA team was unable to recover the space capsule.

words.definition: to know by report; unconfirmed; supposedly
words.example: The students reportedly sent a representative, but she has not yet arrived.
words.zh: 透過報告了解；未經證實；據推測

words.definition: a change in position or direction
to be subject to influence; capable of being affected by a person or thing
words.example: When traveling in tropical climates, travelers are susceptible to malaria.
words.zh: 受到影響；能夠受到人或事物的影響
